title: Three Major Chords
description: Play C, F and G major, the three chords that carry a huge number of songs in the key of C.

steps.title: What makes a chord major
steps.description: A major chord has three notes: the root, the note four half steps above it (the major third), and the note seven half steps above the root (the fifth). On the white keys it often looks like play one, skip one, play one, skip one, play one. Major chords sound bright and settled.

steps.title: C major
steps.description: Play C, E and G together. Use your thumb, middle finger and pinky, skipping a white key between each.
steps.hint: Any C, E and G count, in any order or octave.

steps.title: F major
steps.description: Slide your hand up to F and play F, A and C. Same shape, same skip-a-key pattern.
steps.hint: Thumb on F, middle finger on A, pinky on C.

steps.title: G major
steps.description: Move up one more white key and play G, B and D. Your hand shape hasn't changed at all.
steps.hint: Thumb on G, middle finger on B, pinky on D.

steps.title: Three chords, a lot of songs
steps.description: In the key of C, these are chords I, IV and V, numbered by the scale note each one starts on. That I-IV-V trio drives a huge amount of rock, pop, blues and country. Try it a few times on your own: C, F, G, and back to C.

steps.title: Back home to C
steps.description: Finish on C major one more time. After F and G, notice how it feels like landing back home.
steps.hint: C, E and G again. Thumb, middle finger, pinky.

steps.title: What's inside?
steps.description: Which three notes make up a major chord?
